blocks.text: Nordtrans receives proof-of-delivery and CMR scans by email, and dispatchers matched each one to its order in the TMS by hand before attaching it to the invoice. We timed a sample: about 4.1 minutes per document across the dispatch team. Velho built the smallest useful version first: an inbox rule, OCR, order-number matching with a fuzzy fallback on reference and vehicle plate, and auto-attachment only above a confidence threshold. Everything else goes to a human queue. There is no write-back into the TMS in this version; the output is a draft attachment list and a CSV import, because the TMS vendor's API had a long lead time.

The pilot ran for five days with one dispatcher. About 71% of documents auto-matched, and on a manual check of 310 documents, 2 were wrong. Handling time, including the queue, dropped to about 1.4 minutes per document in that week. Handwritten PODs remained hard for OCR, with roughly 12% of documents routed to the human queue (estimate from the pilot notes).

Adoption went beyond the pilot: all three dispatchers were using the tool by week four, and the team reviews missed matches for 15 minutes each week. The dispatcher who first doubted the approach later asked for the same treatment on export documents, which is a possible next step, not a committed one.

What is still unknown: the invoice lead-time gain comes from a single pilot week and a small sample; the baseline of 7.3% mismatches was not re-measured after launch; customer satisfaction was not tracked. Threshold tuning, miss logging and a Finnish handover document are open work items.

sourceRecord.text:
Client: Nordtrans Oy
Project owner: Aino Rautavaara
kickoff ma 2.9. w/ ops mgr Pekka + 2 dispatchers (Tiina, Joonas)
- problem: POD/CMR scans arrive by email, ppl match manually to orders in TMS -> then attach to invoice. ~ 220 docs/day
- baseline (timed 3 days, Tiina+Joonas): avg 4.1 min/doc, total ~15 h/day?? Pekka says 'ei se niin paljon ole' -> using measured 4.1 min
- mismatch/wrong attachment rate in sample of 300 invoices: 7.3% (22). customer complaints re late invoicing = common
- smallest build: email inbox rule -> OCR + order# regex + fuzzy fallback on ref/plate -> auto-attach if conf > 0.9, else queue in sheet for human
- NO TMS write-back in v1, only draft attachment list + CSV import (TMS vendor API = 6 wk wait, skip)
- wk2: OCR on handwritten POD = rubbish for ~12% docs. added 'needs human' queue, ok
- wk3 pilot w/ Tiina only. 5 days. auto-matched 71% of docs, of which 2 wrong out of 310 checked (0.6%)
- avg handling time after (incl. queue): 1.4 min/doc
- invoice lead time delivery->invoice sent: 5.2 d -> 3.1 d (measured on 140 invoices, pilot wk only so small sample)
- Joonas skeptical at first, then asked for same on export docs. Pekka 'tää on kyllä hyvä'
- adoption: 3/3 dispatchers using by wk4; weekly 15 min review of queue misses
- claim from Pekka: customers 'happier' - not measured, no CSAT data
- TODO: threshold tuning, log misses, handover doc in Finnish. Next: export docs (EUR.1) maybe
